text:
sam_support: @nidhi ACME opened a P0 — they've been seeing intermittent p99 spikes to ~3.2s on hosted endpoints since yesterday's batching policy rollout. p95 looks fine (~180ms). Ticket: https://support.redwood/acme/INC-4821 :face_with_thermometer:

observability-bot: grafana snapshot -> https://grafana.redwood.org/d/abcd/p99-tail?orgId=1&from=7091111200&to=7091112400 — big stair step around 09:12 UTC correlating with config push.

nidhi_sre: seeing same. quick look at batcher metrics: average batch size down to 1.2 for that tenant on some nodes, hold_window_ms is currently 200ms after the rollout. lots of tiny requests = head-of-line wait.

maria_support: repro steps from the customer attached: they send a lot of very short prompts (~10-20 tokens) with high concurrency from a single API key. they also reported no auth/billing errors.

alex_platform: hypothesis: adaptive batching policy change increased max_hold for small-flow to capture bigger batches, but when traffic is very spiky and dominated by tiny prompts we end up with singletons waiting longer. tradeoff: throughput vs tail latency.

sre_oncall: quick mitigation suggestion: 1) enable tiny_request_bypass for that tenant (short-circuit batching for <=32 tokens) 2) reduce hold_window_ms to 40ms for the tenant group 3) canary the change on 2 nodes first. This should lower p99 at cost of a few % token efficiency.

ops_bot: current config (post-rollout):

```
continuous_batcher:
  hold_window_ms: 200
  max_batch_size: 256
  tiny_request_threshold_tokens: 32
  tiny_request_bypass: false
  adaptive_coalesce: true
```

nidhi_sre: logs from one affected GPU host (snip):

```
[2026-03-17T09:12:07Z] batcher: enqueue req tenant=acme size=18 tokens hold_deadline=+200ms
[2026-03-17T09:12:07Z] batcher: dispatch batch_size=1 latency=2034ms reason=hold_timeout
[2026-03-17T09:12:10Z] batcher: enqueue req tenant=acme size=12 tokens hold_deadline=+200ms
[2026-03-17T09:12:10Z] batcher: dispatch batch_size=1 latency=3101ms reason=hold_timeout
```

maria_support: repro script we ran locally (small prompt flood):

```
for i in $(seq 1 800); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
wait
```

nidhi_sre: running that against staging reproduced p99 ~2.8s with current config. if we toggle tiny_request_bypass=true for tenant 'acme' p99 drops to ~240ms in the same run.

sre_oncall: patch commands for canary (example):

```
# patch config for tenant group acme on configmap
kubectl -n inference patch configmap batcher-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/continuous_batcher/hold_window_ms","value":"40"}]'
# or using infra CLI
infractl configs set continuous_batcher.hold_window_ms=40 --tenant=acme --canary=2
```

alex_platform: canary plan: apply to 2 nodes in eu-west first, monitor p95/p99 and token cost for 20m. If p99 improves and cost delta < 6%, promote. If regress, rollback to 200ms.

maria_support: FYI I've replied to ACME letting them know we're investigating and proposing a short-term patch (tiny_request_bypass + reduce hold_window). asked them to pause any client-side retries.

nidhi_sre: longer term options to avoid this taxonomy of tradeoffs: 1) smarter tiny-request classifier so we don't wait to form large batches for obviously tiny prompts 2) tenant-level overrides by traffic shape 3) per-route QoS (latency-sensitive vs throughput-sensitive).

sre_oncall: immediate action items:
- @alex_platform -> schedule canary and run the infractl canary patch (ETA 10m)
- @nidhi_sre -> hotpatch the config if canary looks good, prepare rollback playbook
- @maria_support -> keep ACME updated + collect client rate/shape logs

ops_bot: alert created: #INC-4821 -> linked to this thread; paging oncall if canary fails.

sam_support: thanks all — please post canary metrics here. :thumbsup:
